mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the cost of capital, increasing the present value of future cash flows and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 4.0%) signals weak labor market conditions, prompting the Federal Reserve to implement monetary easing that boosts equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0%, or the correlation between UNRATE > 4.0% and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate weakening consumer demand, reducing corporate earnings expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 0.5% and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns in > 60% of cases (i.e., 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an imminent economic slowdown, reducing corporate profit growth and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The INDPRO decline signal fails to predict negative returns in > 60% of late-cycle expansion instances (i.e., 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1.5% in the last month signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing immediate equity market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The FEDFUNDS increase signal fails to predict negative 5-day returns in > 60% of cases (i.e., 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.0% for 3 months signals a deteriorating labor market, leading to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The UNRATE > 4.0% for 3 months signal fails to predict negative 60-day returns in > 60% of cases (i.e., 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances).

mechanism_narrative: A high level of retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, supporting corporate earnings growth and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in high RSAFS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment (UNRATE) and declines in employment (PAYEMS) indicate a weakening labor market, reducing consumer spending and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increase > 0.2% and PAYEMS decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint UNRATE increase and PAYEMS decline signal fails to predict negative returns in > 60% of cases (i.e., 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances).
